tier_reason: README states 'about 15 percent faster' build and 'about 10 percent faster' query vs nanoflann from the author's own measurements; benchmark.cpp in the repo times both, but no output, CPU, compiler or flags are published, so first-party C.

corrections.workload: benchmark.cpp: 1,000,000 uniform random 3D float points in [-1,1]^3; tree construction timed 10 times; 10,000 random single nearest-neighbour (k=1) queries, each wrapped in its own ScopedTimer; nanoflann KDTreeSingleIndexAdaptor with max leaf size 10 as the comparison.
corrections.caveats: Two-sentence README claim from 'my measurements'; benchmark.cpp (1M uniform random 3D points, 10k 1-NN queries, nanoflann leaf size 10) exists but no results, hardware, compiler or flags are published, and per-query timing with a scoped timer adds overhead to both sides. Tied to Magnum/Corrade types. No LICENSE file (LICENSE, LICENSE.txt, LICENSE.md, COPYING all 404; no licence header in kdtree.h), so reference only. nanoflann is not a listed incumbent here.

notes: Small (11 stars, 9 commits, all June 2020) but has a real side-by-side benchmark file against nanoflann, so tier C rather than D. Metadata (stars, last commit 2020-06-18, no license, not a fork) checked on github.com.

tier_reason: README only states 'On the average, libnabo is 5% to 20% faster than ANN' with no methodology; tests/knnbench.cpp benchmarks ANN when it is installed but publishes no results, CPU or flags, and the cited JOSER 2012 paper (which could raise this to B) could not be opened from this container.

corrections.baseline: ANN (Approximate Nearest Neighbor library, exact-search kd-tree); tests/knnbench.cpp benchmarks ANN (stack and priority search) when ANN is installed. A FLANN code path exists but is switched off in knnbench.cpp ('currently disable FLANN', #undef HAVE_FLANN).
corrections.caveats: README claim only ('5% to 20% faster than ANN'), no published benchmark output, hardware, compiler or flags. Numbers presumably sit in the cited peer-reviewed paper (Elseberg, Magnenat, Siegwart, Nuechter, 'Comparison of nearest-neighbor-search strategies and implementations for efficient shape registration', JOSER 3(1) 2012, doi 10.6092/JOSER_2012_03_01_P2), co-authored by the libnabo author; it was not opened (doi.org, the author's site and uni-wuerzburg.de are blocked here), so tier C until someone reads it. 'make test' runs tests/knnbench.cpp on a bundled 3D scan (K=1/10/30) against ANN if installed; FLANN comparison is disabled in that file. The repo was transferred from ethz-asl (github.com/ethz-asl/libnabo redirects to norlab-ulaval/libnabo); it is not a fork. ANN is not a listed incumbent here.

notes: Metadata checked on github.com: 489 stars, BSD-3-Clause (LICENSE file read), not a fork, not archived, last master commit 2025-07-16 (stale is right). An enricher with access to the JOSER paper should check whether it shows the libnabo-over-ANN win; if it does, B is justified.

tier_reason: README Performance section is a single chart (chart.png) of build and 1spp@720p render times vs Embree 3.13, nanort and Fast-BVH; the record's approximate readings match the chart, but no CPU, compiler, flags, thread count or scene is stated and the competitor harness is not in the repo, so first-party C.

corrections.workload: BVH build time and primary-ray render time (1 spp at 720p) on one unnamed .obj scene, comparing BVH v2 presets (low/medium/high) and BVH v1 builders with Embree 3.13, nanort (2022-08-01, 28bebb8f) and Fast-BVH (2020-03-30, e5366678). The chart does not name the scene (the README's Blend Swap credit is for the example render image).
corrections.caveats: Numbers are only in a chart image (chart.png): no CPU, compiler, flags, thread count or scene named. test/benchmark.cpp benchmarks only this library; the harness used for Embree, nanort and Fast-BVH is not in the repo. Competitor versions on the chart date it to 2022 or later. It beats the simple header-only libraries (nanort, Fast-BVH) but not the real incumbent Embree, which is faster on both build and render. Ray-tracing BVH is only loosely within geometry-spatial; none of this category's named baselines (Boost.Geometry, CGAL, GEOS, R-trees) is compared.

notes: Chart readings checked: v2 medium about 150 ms build / 275 ms render, nanort about 360/645, Fast-BVH about 460/1225, Embree 3.13 about 70/170. Metadata checked on github.com: 1.2k stars, MIT (LICENSE.txt), not a fork, last commit 2026-09-21.
